title: How Well Do LLMs Identify Cultural Unity in Diversity?
findings: The study evaluated LLMs on identifying cultural similarity, where religious aspects were one component of the feature set. Key findings were general to the cultural task: human performance significantly outstripped LLMs, GPT-3.5 performed better than LLaMA models, Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting improved accuracy, and models struggled with less common (long-tail) cultural concepts. The paper did not provide specific findings analyzing model performance on the religious features versus other cultural features.

measurement_description: The benchmark (CUNIT) measured LLMs' ability to identify cultural similarity between concepts, specifically clothing and food items. This measurement included using religious attributes as features for comparison, such as religious occasions (e.g., Christmas, Passover, Deepavali, Lebaran), meanings (e.g., religious beliefs, spiritual), and practices (e.g., worship ancestor).
